name: Sugi no Osugi

location.address: Yasaka Shrine, Sugi, Otoyo, Nagaoka District, Kochi Prefecture

access: Paid entry, 200 yen per adult, which funds the tree's own protection; free for the walk to the shrine grounds otherwise. Roughly 800 metres on foot from Osugi Station on JR Shikoku's Dozan Line.
transport: 800 metres on foot from JR Shikoku Dozan Line's Osugi Station, named after the tree itself.
verify_notes: Standalone destination tree, one of Japan's largest cedars: two fused trunks growing from one base at Yasaka Shrine, known as Minami Osugi (south, root-circumference approx 20m, height approx 60m) and Kita Osugi (north, root-circumference approx 16.5m, height approx 56-57m), together nicknamed 'Meoto Sugi' (married-couple cedar). Legend attributes its planting to the god Susanoo. Designated National Natural Monument in 1924, upgraded to Special Natural Monument in 1952 (one of Japan's highest tree designations), and selected for the 'New Japan Famous Trees 100' list in 1990. girth_cm records the larger south trunk's root-level circumference (roughly 20m); this is a root-level figure rather than a standard breast-height girth, noted here so the writer does not repeat it as a trunk measurement. Current concern is root compaction from heavy visitor foot traffic near the base rather than disease; Otoyo Town runs active conservation with prefectural and national support, funded partly by the 200 yen entry fee. Flagged because the age (roughly 3,000 years) is a traditional/legendary estimate rather than a scientific dating.
